Abstract— Small retail businesses often rely on manual 
inventory management practices that lead to data inaccuracies 
and operational inefficiencies. This study presents Stock Easy, a 
lightweight mobile application designed to support inventory 
management and facilitate digital transformation among small 
retail businesses. The application was developed using a user-
centered design approach and includes core functions such as 
product data management, stock tracking, and inventory 
updates. A quantitative evaluation was conducted with 132 
users, including retail owners, online sellers, store managers, 
and inventory staff. Data were collected using a structured 
questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics and 
Pearson correlation analysis. The results indicate high user 
satisfaction, particularly in terms of ease of use (mean = 4.52), 
process clarity (mean = 4.41), and user interface design (mean = 
4.36). Correlation analysis further reveals that perceived ease of 
use and perceived usefulness significantly influence overall 
satisfaction, which is positively associated with perceived 
readiness 
for 
digital 
transformation. 
These 
findings 
demonstrate that lightweight digital tools such as Stock Easy can 
effectively improve inventory management practices and serve 
as an entry point for digital transformation in small retail 
businesses. 
Keywords— Digital Transformation, Inventory Management, 
Mobile Application, Small Retail Businesses, User Satisfaction, 
Technology Adoption 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Digital transformation (DT) has become a key driver of 
competitiveness and operational efficiency for businesses 
worldwide [1]-[2]. In the context of small and medium-sized 
enterprises (SMEs), the adoption of digital technologies can 
significantly improve productivity, decision-making, and 
supply chain management [3]. 
In Thailand, SMEs represent more than 99% of all 
enterprises and employ over 85% of the workforce, making 
them essential contributors to national economic development 
[4]. Despite their importance, many small retail businesses 
still rely on manual processes for operational management, 
particularly in inventory control [5]. Such traditional 
approaches often result in data inaccuracies, stock shortages, 
overstock situations, and inefficiencies in business operations 
[6]. Previous studies emphasize that digital transformation in 
SMEs should not necessarily begin with complex enterprise 
systems but rather with lightweight digital tools that align with 
the operational context and technological capabilities of small 
businesses [7]-[8]. Inventory management systems, for 
example, can improve data transparency, reduce operational 
errors, and support better planning and decision-making [8]. 
 
However, empirical studies focusing on user-centered 
digital tools tailored for small retail businesses in developing 
countries remain limited. Many existing systems are either too 
complex or costly for small retailers to adopt effectively. To 
address this gap, this study introduces Stock Easy, a mobile 
application designed to support inventory management and 
promote digital transformation among small retail businesses 
as in Fig. 1. The application focuses on essential functions that 
simplify stock monitoring and improve data management in 
everyday operations.  
 
Fig. 1. Conceptual Framework (TAM + Digital Transformation). 
The objectives of this study are: 1) To develop a mobile 
application (Stock Easy) for inventory management in small 
retail businesses. 2) To evaluate user satisfaction and usability 
of the application. 3) To investigate the role of the application 
in supporting digital transformation readiness. 4) To analyze 
the relationships between technology acceptance factors and 
user satisfaction.

III. METHODOLOGY 
A. System Development 
The Stock Easy application was developed using a user-
centered design approach to ensure usability for small retail 
business operators with varying levels of digital literacy as 
show in Fig. 2.

The system supports the following core functions: 
• 
Product data management (product ID, product 
name, stock quantity) 
• 
Expiration date tracking 
• 
Product image storage 
• 
Product search functionality 
• 
Add, edit, and delete inventory records

These functions aim to simplify inventory management 
tasks while reducing reliance on manual record-keeping. 
B. Participants 
 The study involved 132 participants who had actual 
experience using the Stock Easy application. The participants 
were categorized into four groups: 
• 
Small retail business owners (31) 
• 
Online sellers (27) 
• 
Shop owners or store managers (41) 
• 
Inventory and frontline staff (33) 
Participants were selected using purposive sampling to 
ensure relevant user experience. 
C. Data Collection Instrument 
The measurement items for key constructs, including 
Perceived Ease of Use (PEOU) and Perceived Usefulness 
(PU), were adapted from the original Technology Acceptance 
Model (TAM) proposed by Davis (1989) and subsequent 
validated studies in SME and mobile application contexts. 
Minor wording adjustments were made to align with the 
inventory management scenario. All items were reviewed by 
three domain experts to ensure contextual relevance prior to 
pilot testing.

Abstract—Demand forecasting plays an important role in 
the food and beverage (FnB) industry by helping businesses 
anticipate customer demand and support operational planning 
during peak periods. This study conducts a comparative 
empirical evaluation of three forecasting models, Seasonal 
Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), FB 
Prophet, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to predict 
hourly demand patterns in a coffee shop environment. The 
models were evaluated using hourly demand patterns in a coffee 
shop environment. The models were evaluated using hourly 
sales data collected from Saudagar Kopi in Jakarta over a three-
month period (April-June 2025). Forecasting performance was 
assessed using Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) as the 
primary evaluation metric. The results indicate that the LSTM 
model achieves the lowest forecasting error and is better able to 
capture abrupt demand spikes and high-frequency fluctuations 
compared with SARIMA and FB Prophet, which perform well 
in modeling trend and seasonality but tend to underestimate 
sudden peak-hour demand. These findings highlight the 
potential of deep learning approaches for modeling complex 
demand patterns in high-frequency time-series data. However, 
the results should be interpreted within the context of a limited 
dataset and a single business environment. Future research may 
explore alternative models that address zero-inflated demand 
patterns and evaluate forecast performance across multiple 
retail locations. 
Keywords—Demand Forecasting, Peak Hours, SARIMA, 
LSTM, FB Prophet. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
The coffee shop industry has expanded rapidly in recent 
years, driven by young consumers and urban professionals 
who increasingly use coffee shops as multifunctional spaces 
for socializing, studying, and remote working. Indonesia, the 
world’s 4th largest coffee produce [1], has a strong coffee 
culture that supports this growth. Coffee, once associated with 
lower-class and middle-class consumption, has evolved into a 
modern lifestyle product with broad market appeal [2], 
positioning coffee shops as an important segment within the 
service economy. 
As customer activities diversify, operational challenges 
arise, particularly during peak hours, when high customer 
traffic can lead to long queues, delayed orders, and 
inconsistent service quality. These issues are evident at 
Saudagar Kopi, a popular coffee shop located in Jakarta’s 
Sabang business district, which attracts office workers on 
weekdays and general visitors on weekends. Peak-hour 
congestion has resulted in service delays and negative 
customer feedback, posing risks to satisfaction, loyalty, and 
business sustainability. 
Demand forecasting provides a strategic approach for 
anticipating customer volume and optimizing operations. 
Accurate forecasting can support improvements in resource 
allocation, inventory management, pricing strategies, and 
promotional planning in retail and food service settings [3] In 
coffee shops, demand prediction may help inform capacity 
management and waiting times, which are key drivers of 
customer satisfaction and loyalty [4] 
Previous studies have implemented various forecasting 
models 
including 
DNN 
(Deep 
Neural 
Networks), 
Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), and 
Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to identify the most 
suitable approach based on data characteristics [5]. LSTM 
models have effectively captured temporal dependencies such 
as seasonality and day-of-week patterns [6] and are widely 
used for intelligent demand planning in modern supply chains 
[7].  
This study investigates operational inefficiencies at 
Saudagar Kopi, a high-traffic coffee shop in Jakarta, 
particularly during peak hours that lead to delayed orders and 
customer dissatisfaction. To address this, the research 
proposes the use of demand forecasting to predict customer 
volume and support operational planning. This study 
examines several forecasting models to determine which 
approach is most suitable for the characteristics of hourly sales 
data. Therefore, this study conducts a comparative empirical 
evaluation of 3 forecasting models, SARIMA, FB Prophet, 
and LSTM to analyze their effectiveness in predicting hourly 
demand patterns in a coffee shop context.

II. LITERATURE REVIEW 
A. Business Overview 
Saudagar Kopi is a coffee shop located on Jl. Sabang No 
26F, Central Jakarta. Established in 2012, the shop specializes 
in strong and bold coffee made from single-origin beans and 
house blends while also offering Indonesian dishes, snacks, 
and packaged roasted beans. Its primary customers include 
coffee enthusiasts and office workers seeking high-quality 
coffee in a comfortable environment.  
Products are sold directly in-store and through delivery 
platforms such as GoFood, GrabFood, and ShopeeFood, while 
roasted beans are sold through online marketplaces. 
Operationally, the Purchasing & Warehouse division manages 
ingredient procurement and inventory, while the kitchen and 
bar request supplies based on daily and weekly needs. 
Currently, production planning relies largely on intuition 
rather than structured forecasting. This research focuses on the 
production process, particularly forecasting demand based on 
food and beverage sales. Figure 1 illustrates the operational 
business process of Saudagar Kopi, highlighting the stages 
where demand forecasting can support production planning 
and preparation during peak demand periods. 
 
Fig. 1. Business Process Diagram of Saudagar Kopi. 
B. Theoretical Foundations of Time Series Forecasting 
1) Demand Forecasting 
Demand Forecasting is an essential component of 
operational planning that enables organizations to estimate 
future demand for products or services. Accurate forecasts can 
support inventory preparation, resource allocation, and 
production planning particularly in industries with fluctuating 
demand such as food and beverage services. Recent studies 
have increasingly applied machine learning and deep learning 
approaches to improve forecasting accuracy. Models such as 
ARIMA, LSTM, and hybrid methods have been widely 
compared across different demand forecasting contexts [8] 
[9]. Deep learning models like LSTM have shown strong 
performance in forecasting complex demand patterns and 
short shelf-life products [10]. 
2) SARIMA Model 
The Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average 
(SARIMA) extends the ARIMA framework by incorporating 
seasonal components to capture recurring patterns in time-
series 
data. 
The 
model 
is 
represented 
as 
SARIMA(p,d,q)(P,D,Q)s, allowing simultaneous modelling 
of non-seasonal dynamics and seasonal behavior. SARIMA 
has been widely applied in forecasting domains such as 
energy demand and economic indicators due to its ability to 
model trend and seasonality effectively [11]. Model 
performance 
depends 
on 
appropriate 
parameter 
identification, typically guided by statistical tools such as 
ACF, PACF, and information criteria [12]. For example, 
Ghodusinejad et al. (2025) applied SARIMA to forecast 
electricity 
and 
gasoline 
demand, 
demonstrating 
its 
effectiveness in identifying long-term demand trends [13]. 
3) LSTM 
Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is a type of Recurrent 
Neural Network (RNN) designed to model sequential data by 
capturing long-term temporal dependencies. Its memory cell 
architecture allows the model to retain relevant information 
from previous time steps, making it suitable for time-series 
forecasting tasks [14]. Recent studies have demonstrated the 
strong forecasting capabilities of LSTM-based models. For 
instance, Yingnan and Xiaowei (2025) showed that an ES-
LSTM model achieved lower forecasting errors compared 
with traditional approaches such as LSSVM and BPNN 
highlighting the effectiveness of LSTM in modelling 
dynamic demand patterns [15]. 
4) FB Prophet 
FB Prophet is a forecasting model developed by Facebook 
to handle time series data with complex seasonality, trend 
changes, and irregular events. The model decomposes time 
series data into trend, seasonal, and holiday components, 
allowing 
it 
to 
capture 
multiple 
seasonal

Abstract— Demand quantity determination plays a crucial 
role in operations management, particularly in improving 
purchasing decisions and stock management. This article 
considers the evaluation of daily demand forecasting 
performance in a food and beverage SME using real data from 
sales trans- actions, focusing on the main ice cream product. The 
methods used include a seven-day moving average (MA(7)) 
baseline model, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model 
without optimization, and an LSTM optimized using a grid 
search approach. Model performance is measured using RMSE 
(Root Mean Squared Error) and MAPE (Mean Absolute 
Percentage Error), but also through unit-based inventory 
simulations to assess operational impact. The study showed that 
the optimized LSTM produced the best performance with an 
RMSE of 1.65 and a MAPE of 45.06%—better than MA(7) with 
an RMSE of 1.84 and a MAPE of 46.60%. From an operational 
perspective, the best LSTM configuration was able to 
completely eliminate lost demand, although it resulted in an 
excess inventory of 1.57 units.

inventory optimization, LSTM, Grid Search, small medium 
enterprise. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Demand forecasting plays a significant role in business 
activities, serving as a basis for operational decisions, 
including inventory management. For example, in the Food 
and Beverage sector, products tend to spoil easily and 
experience fluctuating demand. Inaccurate forecasting can 
result in losses: insufficient inventory leads to lost sales 
opportunities, while excess storage increases the risk of 
spoilage. 
Efficiency in inventory management plays a crucial role in 
establishing a source of competitive advantage for businesses; 
companies that are able to more accurately align stock levels 
with demand patterns generally operate more effectively and 
efficiently [1]. In the context of small and medium- sized 
enterprises (SMEs), the ability to reliably forecast demand is 
key to survival and competition in an increasingly competitive 
marketplace. 
Most small businesses (SMEs) often base their purchasing 
and inventory procurement decisions on intuition and the 
owner’s experience [2] . This approach carries the potential 
for significant losses, particularly when demand patterns 
experience unexpected changes or fluctuations. This 
demonstrates the need for a more systematic, data-driven 
approach to demand forecasting to support operational 
decision-making in SMEs. 
This research utilized a real sales transaction dataset 
obtained from a micro and small enterprise (SME) operating 
in the food and beverage sector. The primary product offered 
by this SME is ice cream, but they also offer a variety of 
complementary food and beverage menu items. The 
transaction data used represents actual daily sales activity, 
thus reflecting the business’s actual operational conditions. 
Therefore, this study examines several time series-based 
forecasting approaches through a comparative study. As a 
baseline method, a seven-day moving average (MA(7)) model 
is applied to represent simple forecasting practices. Next, a 
Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model is tested as a deep 
learning approach to capture more complex temporal patterns 
in daily sales data. Furthermore, this study also examines the 
hyperparameter optimization process in the LSTM model to 
improve forecasting performance. 
II. RELATED WORK 
In the context of operations management, it is important to 
consider the relationship between inventory decisions and the 
quality of projected demand information. Forecasting acts as 
an initial mechanism that transforms historical data into 
estimates of future product needs, so that procurement can be 
managed more systematically and in a controlled manner [3], 
[4]. Furthermore, these projections are used as one of the main 
sources in operational decision making, for example in 
determining order quantities, setting rescheduling, and 
adjusting inventory levels to stay in line with actual demand 
patterns [5]. 
The moving average method is a basic forecasting 
approach that builds predictions based on the average demand 
value over several previous periods. The algorithm’s 
practicality and simplicity make this method often chosen by 
practitioners due to its ease of implementation and low 
computational 
requirements. 
In 
addition 
to 
demand 
forecasting, moving averages are also popular in technical 
analysis of financial markets due to their relevance in 
identifying price trends and supporting trading decision-
making through analysis of historical price movement 
patterns. [6]. 
According to Ananth et al. [7] research, simple forecasting 
approaches remain relevant for sales prediction because they 
found that by using Simple Moving Average and Simple 
Linear Regression, historical average-based estimates are able 
to provide competitive levels of accuracy without having to 
rely on more complex models.

Unlike simple statistical approaches, Long Short-Term

con- trolled by a gate mechanism, namely input gates, forget 
gates, and output gates, this model is able to regulate the flow 
of information across time. This mechanism allows the 
network to determine for itself which information to retain, 
ignore, or pass on to the next period. This capability makes 
LSTM very effective in modeling complex temporal 
dynamics, including time series forecasting problems. [8], [9]. 
In the context of automotive pricing, Long et al. (2023) 
proposed a hybrid GM(1,1)-LSTM approach and compared 
the results; their study concluded that the combination of 
traditional pre- diction methods and LSTM tends to improve 
forecasting accuracy while maintaining sensitivity to external 
economic fluctuations. In the retail sec- tor, Kaunchi et al.

most appropriate combination of setting parameters so that the 
model can operate optimally on the data used [10]. 
Hyperparameter optimization is a crucial factor in 
improving the performance of machine learning models, 
including neural network-based algorithms such as LSTM. 
Siregar et al. demonstrated that a combination of grid search 
and random search can improve the accuracy of classification 
models by reducing reliance on manual parameter 
determination [11]. In the context of time series forecasting,

by

III. METHODOLOGY 
This study uses the Point of Sale (POS) system of a micro 
and small enterprise (SME) in the food and beverage sector as 
a data source. Its operational pattern is similar to the business 
model of an established franchised ice cream outlet. The data 
set was collected continuously from March 2023 to the end of 
December 2025, thus covering a fairly long medium-term 
sales observation period. The choice of daily data resolution 
aligns with the management practices of small business 
owners in planning raw material purchases and inventory 
control. 
The analysis focuses on a single product, vanilla ice 
cream, which serves as the core product and exhibits a 
consistent sales pattern since the business began. This ice 
cream was selected due to its complete data and relatively 
stable sales pattern, suitable for use in time series analysis. 
After calendar alignment and handling of non-transaction 
days, the final dataset used in this study consisted of 
approximately 1,030 daily observation points. 
In this study, the forecasting objective is vanilla ice cream 
sales, represented by monthly aggregation, as shown in Figure 
1. In the early stages of business operations, sales fluctuations 
appeared relatively high, particularly in mid-2023. Over time, 
sales patterns showed a more controlled tendency, although 
seasonal variations were mild and changes in direction 
between periods still occurred sporadically.

Abstract—This study investigates how technology and 
organization factors related to the technology organization and 
external (TOE) model (technological, organizational, and 
environmental) affect how auditors perceive and use artificial 
intelligence (AI) tools and the resulting quality of audits 
performed. The study also uses the technology acceptance model 
(TAM) to assess audit quality resulting from the use of AI tools, 
using survey data collected from 120 auditors at small and 
medium sized companies in Thailand. The data was analyzed 
using basic stats and structural equation modelling (partial least 
squares - structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with 
ADANCO 2.4.1 and 5000 bootstrapping iterations). Results 
indicate that the measurement tool reached acceptable levels of 
reliability and convergent validity. The structural model's 
results linked the independent variables to significant variance 
in perceived AI benefits (73.73%) and AI acceptance and use 
(71.24%). The variance in the dependent variable of perceived 
ease, usefulness, and audit quality used AI tools were very low. 
Hypothesis tests showed that there was a statistically significant 
and positive relationship between environmental factors and 
perceived benefits of AI based on legal regulations (β = 0.562, p 
< .05) while all other independent variable factors were 
estimated to have no statistically predictable relationship with 
perceived benefits of using AI for auditing. Thus, the findings 
provide useful information for auditors regarding the effects on 
audit success of adopting new technology. These findings can 
also aid organizations, regulatory agencies, and the Federation 
of Accounting Professions in developing a plan to support the 
use of new technologies. 
Keywords—technology-organization-environment 
framework, technology acceptance model, artificial intelligence, 
auditing, audit quality  
I. 
INTRODUCTION 
Currently, the industrial sector in Thailand is preparing in 
all aspects to accommodate technological changes that affect 
work systems, data storage, and service delivery, to promote 
and facilitate organizations and increase work efficiency [1]. 
According to regulations, all industrial entities in Thailand are 
required to prepare financial statements and income 
statements for auditing and presentation to an auditor for 
approval at a meeting during every accounting period [2]. The 
purpose of auditing is to express an opinion that the financial 
statements are fairly accurate in all material respects in 
accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. 
Auditing requires obtaining sufficient and appropriate 
evidence to achieve reasonable assurance in expressing an 
opinion [3]. With the transition of legal entities to digital 
operations, there is an increase in the volume of data being 
generated and stored, creating more complex data structures. 
Furthermore, traditional methods used for auditing are no 
longer adequate in providing sufficient and pertinent evidence 
for the purposes of auditing; therefore, there is a need to 
augment auditing processes through the application of 
Artificial Intelligence (AI). 
The use of AI has greatly enhanced how audits are 
performed by enabling auditors to analyze large amounts of 
information at a rapid speed, which improves the accuracy in 
identifying risks and anomalies and providing better 
evaluation of audit evidence that can lead to higher quality 
audits; however, auditors can only maximize the advantages 
of using such technology if they understand what influences 
their level of acceptance and utilization of it. Therefore, this 
study is designed to examine the factors that influence audit 
quality in the way that auditors in Thailand utilize AI as a 
source of support, especially for those who belong to medium 
and small audit firms. In addition to identifying these factors 
using a technology, organization and environment framework, 
the study will also consider how technology acceptance theory 
affects the factors identified in the study. The results of this 
research will allow audit firms, auditors and the Federation of 
Accounting Professions to develop strategies to improve the 
way that auditors use AI.

the introduction of IOT, Big Data, and other key technologies. 
By utilizing things like Blockchain [7], RPA, Machine 
Learning [8], Big Data, Cloud Computing, and Deep Learning

B. Audit Quality 
According to International Auditing and Assurance 
Standards Board (IAASB) [18], auditors must indicate 
whether the financial statements are materially misstated 
based on sound and appropriate evidence. Such audits must 
follow specified Standards to ensure that users of the financial 
statements have the highest degree of assurance. 
The quality of an audit consists of three components: 1) 
Inputs – consist of the qualities of the auditors themselves 
(ethics, integrity, independence, and competence) as well as 
the way the audit team manages and understands the clients' 
business under the audit firm's quality-control policies and 
systems (International Standards for Quality Control 1 and 2), 
2) Procedures – consist of those procedures required by the 
IAASB [19-20] in relation to compliance with standards and 
laws, including planning, risk assessment, evidence-
gathering, application of technology, and continuous 
improvement through communication with clients and 3) 
Outcomes – of the audit are reported in the form of an 
unqualified audit report that demonstrates an audit's ability to 
meet the needs of its users by instilling confidence, furthering 
internal controls, enhancing financial reporting processes, 
providing useful information to stakeholders to support their 
decision-making processes, and ultimately creating business 
value. 
Quality inspection is based on inputs, standard procedures, 
and the use of technology for the creation of reports that are 
complete, trustworthy, and useful to all interested parties for 
making decisions. 
C. Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) 
In 1989, Fred Davis proposed the Technology Acceptance 
Model (TAM) that attempts to describe and predict whether or 
not people will utilize new technology. There are two basic 
drivers to deciding to accept/use technology - perceived 
benefits of enhancing efficiency/effectiveness through use of 
the technology, and perceived ease of use of the technology. 
Both of these drivers are influenced by other outside factors 
that ultimately impact user's perceptions and ultimately their 
intentions towards using the technology. 
TAM evolved into TAM2 [21] through the incorporation 
of social, organizational and work-related factors – including 
social norms, image, job relevance and outcome quality - that 
contribute to the explanation of how technology can be 
accepted/made use of within organizations. Further, it evolved 
into TAM3 with the addition of psychological and 
competency-related factors (including self efficacy, anxiety 
and previous experience) that influence perceived ease of use. 
TAM has been continuously refined to provide a richer 
definition and description of user behavior in an increasingly 
technologically complex world. 
Researchers are developing new variations of and 
iterations to the various TAM models, and researchers are 
continually working to develop new variables or variables 
appropriate for their particular area of study. 
D. Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) 
Framework 
The Tornatzky and Fleischer (1990) technology-
organizational-environment (TOE) framework provides 
researchers a means of understanding the different factors that 
can influence technology adoption by organizations. The TOE 
framework 
uses 
three 
dimensions 
(technological, 
organizational, and external environment) to assess the impact 
of technology on organizations. Each of these three 
dimensions will influence both an organization’s ability to 
adopt innovative technologies, as well as the overall success 
that the organization has in the implementation and use of new 
technology. 
The TOE framework provides researchers with a high 
degree of flexibility to allow researchers to choose the specific 
sub-factors that are applicable to a particular context. For 
example, [22] used the TOE framework to study the adoption 
of A.I. by small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and were 
able to determine the following factors as significant: 1) 
Technological (competitive advantage and value), 2) 
Compatibility (conformity with existing processes and 
culture), 3) Organizational (readiness and capability of human 
resources), and 4) Environmental (market demand, external 
pressures, and support from the Government). 
In addition to leveraging the flexibility of the TOE 
framework, the researchers also conducted a literature review 
to identify the factors affecting the use of A.I. applications in 
the quality of audit work.

management in food and beverage business based
on retailing is accurate demand forecasting. This
paper will attempt to forecast hourly ice cream

There are numerous huge franchise brands with

enterprises in such a scenario are left to han-

sustain and expand their businesses. An effective

opportunities [2].

accurately predict and estimate the daily, weekly
and monthly product demand. This facilitates bet-
ter buying decisions of the raw materials and min-
imize chances of overstocking or understocking.
Adjustment of production activities can be also
optimized more accurately that helps in optimiza-
tion of the operational processes and provide quick
response to changes in the market. [3].

and accurate in predicting inventory demand in
small-scale enterprises and enhancing operational

II. RELATED WORK
Long Short-Term Memory networks are recur-
rent neural networks that overcome the weak-
nesses of the traditional recurrent systems, namely,
the vanishing and exploding gradient issues that
constrain the property of recurrent models of
simulating long-range connectivity of sequential
information. The networks make use of a unique
structure that incorporates nodes and a gating
mechanism that regulates a flow of information
into, within or out of the cell. This architec-
ture makes Long Short-term Memory networks to
shine in problems involving modeling of tempo-
ral sequence like speech recognition, handwriting
recognition and natural language processing tasks
[4]. The model capacity is also improved by the
bidirectional and stacked extensions as well as the
contextual information contributed by the architec-
tural extensions of the model [5]. These benefits
notwithstanding, Long Short-Term Memory net-
works are computationally expensive and this is
a problem with the implementation on resource-
constrained systems. Efforts to alleviate this inter-
est in doing away with redundant computation and
hardware accelerator to enhance efficiency. [6].
Some studies have applied Long Short-Term
Memory networks to forecast sales, demand of
products or inventory of groceries and have shown
that the networks considerably enhance the accu-
racy of the prediction in various retailing envi-
ronments. These models are useful in modeling
time dependent relationships and nonlinear trends
that are common with sales data and can be easily
defeated by traditional statistical methods. As il-
lustrated by Agrahari [7], Long Short-Term Mem-
ory architectures have an advantage over linear
regressions and decision tree models in that they
are better-adjusted to time-series behavior, leading
to better sales forecasting and more responsive
business decisions.
In another study, Subhalakshmi et al. [8] devel-
oped a Long Short-Term Memory based predic-
tion model of supermarkets, which was far more
successful as it acknowledged variables such as
store type, date, and item level sales and therefore
it was more successful in inventory management
and it was in a position to eliminate overstocking
or stockouts losses. In the e-grocery domain, Go-
labek et al. [?] discovered that Long Short-Term
Memory models were more accurate compared
to machine learning and statistical models, but
random forest and linear regression were slightly
more accurate on beverages only. The implication
of these findings is that the product-level demand
forecasting with the help of Long Short-Term
Memory networks offers a valid approach of in-
ventory control and customer demand fulfillment.
One of the most common methods is naive
forecasting [9] in which the value forecasted in
the next period would be identical to the value
that has been observed in the previous period.
This method, no matter how simple it is, can
sometimes work quite well with data with strong
short-term correlations, such as the hourly loads
in food and drinks retail [10]. In addition to this
method, moving averages are also typically used
as a baseline to an extent of smoothing out short
term variation and also identify local trends [11].
The event of interest in the study was the sales
average of the last seven hours (MA7) because this
is the time period of the demand dynamics of the
cafe within one daily cycle of activity. However,
the approach is less efficient in reflecting recurrent
routine seasonal patterns.
To correct this deficiency, the daily seasonal
naive method [12] was used as a comparison also.
It is a forecasting method which predicts demand
using the value at the same hour of the day before,
and it is also particularly relevant where the data
has a strong daily seasonal cycle. This method
suits well to hourly Point-of-Sale (POS) data, as
customer demand patterns tend to stay constant on
a day to day basis. Having the three baselines of
naive forecast, MA7 and daily seasonal naive in
place, the study provides further argument that the
increased performance of the LSTM model could
not be explained by the complexity of the model,
but by the ability to capture more complex patterns
in the product demand data, both time and season.

Abstract— Small shops and retail stores in Peru face 
significant challenges in efficient management due to limited 
access to technological resources, often relying on error-prone 
manual processes. This study presents the development of a 
mobile application powered by the GPT-4 model, designed to 
provide personalized recommendations and optimize key 
operations such as inventory management and sales forecasting. 
By leveraging GPT-4’s advanced natural language processing 
capabilities, the application acts as an intelligent assistant, 
enabling shop owners to make informed decisions, automate 
routine tasks, and enhance business performance. Key features 
include 
product 
and 
sales 
management, 
dashboards, 
personalized recommendations, alerts, and other operational 
tools. A survey conducted with 15 shop owners revealed positive 
results, with over 66.7% rating the application between 4 and 5 
on a Likert scale (1-5), indicating its effectiveness in improving 
small shop management with the support of GPT-4. 
Keywords— GPT-4, Management, Small Shops, Chatbot, 
Assistant 
I. INTRODUCTION 
In recent years, the management of small-scale retail 
establishments, such as small shops and stores, has posed 
significant challenges in the Peruvian context. These 
challenges stem from several factors, including limited access 
to technological resources, leading to a reliance on manual 
processes for inventory management, decision making, and 
performance evaluation [1]. The absence of efficient 
technological solutions exposes shop owners to errors in 
calculations, uninformed decision making, and suboptimal 
business performance [2]. This generates operational 
problems that negatively affect their performance, such as 
performing error-prone manual calculations for routine tasks, 
inventory control using rudimentary methods, and strategic 
decision making hampered by the lack of reliable data and 
analytical tools [3], [4], [5]. These limitations prevent small 
shop owners from realizing the full potential of their business 
and making informed decisions to improve their profitability 
and competitiveness in the marketplace.  
This research aims to explore the potential of AI-driven 
approaches to improve the management of small shops in 
Peru. By leveraging the capabilities of GPT-4, the goal is to 
develop a mobile application that serves as an intelligent 
management tool for shop owners to manage their businesses, 
make informed decisions, and optimize their business 
operations. In that sense, with the integration of GPT-4, the 
application will provide personalized recommendations based 
on data from the small shop and an intelligent chatbot that 
provides instant access to information from the small shop, as 
well as serving as a management assistant. 
II. LITERATURE REVIEW 
A. GPT and Large Language Model 
The capabilities that AI technology contains are useful for 
various domains, in the case of the research focuses on the use 
of GPT's LLM model. For example, GPT demonstrates a 
robust ability to understand and generate natural language 
fluently. This is achieved thanks to its architecture of attention 
neural networks or "transformers" and the pre-training of 1 
trillion parameters as in GPT-4 [6]. On the other hand, 
according to Keng-Boon's study, generative AI is being used 
in retail, so that it enables customers to have faster service and 
improved employee productivity [7]. In addition, Kurnia 
Muludi considers GPT as one of the best LLM models [8], 
because of the results she obtained in her research. Also, 
according to Amos Azaria, he highlights its ability to be used 
in scientific research, mathematics, programming, education 
and health care [9].  
On the other hand, there are many LLM models, which can 
be open source or closed source. Each of these is trained with 
different data sizes, so the accuracy differs in each one.  For 
this reason, Samuel Kernan's study compares different LLM 
models using different performance criteria [10]. These 
criteria are Factuality which refers to whether the generated 
answers are correct according to the context, Completeness 
which refers to whether the answers contain all the relevant 
information of the question and Hallucinations which refers to 
whether the answer is coherent according to the question. The 
study concludes that GPT-4 shows the best performance 
compared to other models. However, open-source models 
such as StableBeluga2 also show similar performances. 
B. GPT applications for recommendation 
GPT has various applications in the health sector. For 
instance, Ismael Dergaa's study utilized OpenAI's GPT-4 
model to generate exercise routines tailored to individual 
goals. While the routines effectively supported fitness, they 
lacked deeper personalization [4]. Another notable use of GPT 
is in early disease detection. A study employing ChatGPT for 
the preliminary diagnosis of dengue fever reported highly 
satisfactory results [11]. Similarly, Li's research developed a 
chatbot leveraging GPT agents to evaluate responses to 
questions about traumatic brain injury rehabilitation [12]. 
Finally, Pash's study demonstrated how a GPT-powered 
chatbot, using patient-provided information, accurately 
identified the appropriate area of care [13].  
The manufacturing sector has also benefited from the 
application of GPT. For example, in Kahiomba's study, a web 
application was developed to process data from production 
machines, enabling GPT to generate responses that help 
technicians identify issues quickly, thereby reducing

III. EXPERIMENTATION 
A. Materials 
The project aims to showcase the potential of a GPT-4-
powered chatbot assistant for optimizing the management of 
small shops. To achieve this, an Android application will be 
developed, enabling shop owners to efficiently handle their 
businesses 
through 
intelligent 
recommendations 
and 
strategies generated by GPT-4. The app will facilitate key 
tasks such as product creation, supplier management, sales 
and purchase tracking, employee management, and dashboard 
visualization. 
By leveraging data provided by shop owners and the GPT-
4 model, the application will deliver personalized queries and 
responses, addressing topics such as shop performance and 
app usage. Additionally, GPT-4 will generate tailored 
business recommendations, including suggested products, 
offers, and discounts, empowering shop owners with 
actionable insights to gain a competitive edge in their markets. 
The application will utilize MongoDB, a non-relational 
database, to store large volumes of data efficiently and with 
optimal latency. A REST API will be developed using NestJS, 
a Node.js framework that employs TypeScript and offers 
modular architecture, ensuring scalability and maintainability. 
Furthermore, the application will integrate external 
services such as Cloudflare R2, OpenAI API, AWS SES, and 
Firebase Cloud Messaging for tasks like static file storage and 
push notifications. Cloud services will also be employed to 
host the API and database, specifically using Google Cloud’s 
Compute Engine and MongoDB Atlas. 
To evaluate the application's impact, a qualitative analysis 
will be conducted through a user survey involving 15 shop 
owners. This survey aims to assess the user experience and 
determine the application’s effectiveness in improving shop 
management. Additionally, it will demonstrate the role of the 
GPT-4 model in enhancing business decision-making and 
operational efficiency. 
B. Methodology 
The project follows a clear methodology to implement the 
mobile application. The application, developed in Java 8, 
interacts with end users to manage various tasks such as 
creating products, managing suppliers, and tracking sales. The 
REST API, developed with NestJS, handles the business logic 
of the application and communicates with both the database 
and external services. MongoDB is used to store the data, and 
the OpenAI API interacts with the GPT-4 model to provide 
personalized recommendations and responses based on the 
shop’s context. 
The GPT-4 model contributes significantly to the research 
by enabling the creation of dynamic, context-aware 
recommendations for shop owners. When a user queries the 
system, the model processes the relevant data retrieved from 
the database, such as product sales and inventory details, and 
generates responses to help improve decision-making. The 
assistant’s ability to interpret the data and provide tailored 
advice is critical for achieving the research objective of 
enhancing small shop management through artificial 
intelligence. 
Additionally, Fig. 1 describes the process in which a user 
interacts with a GPT-based assistant. It begins when the user 
asks a question. The relevant data is retrieved from the 
database and saved, with a JSON file containing the obtained 
data. Then, a vector store is created, and the JSON file is 
uploaded to the vector store. A thread is created with the user's 
message, and the assistant executes the thread to process the 
query. If the response is satisfactory, the process ends; if not, 
the user can make another query, and the process repeats.

IV. CONCLUSIONS 
In this paper, the design and development of a mobile 
application for the intelligent management of small shops 
using the GPT-4 model has been presented. During the study, 
the system architecture was proposed and a detailed flow of 
interaction with the GPT-4 model was elaborated. 
According to the survey of 15 shop owners and employees, 
the application proved to be useful, interactive, and easy to 
use. The GPT-4 model has enabled shop owners to query their 
shop data in an efficient and interactive way, significantly 
improving data accessibility and providing quick, accurate 
responses. The intuitive user interface has enhanced the user 
experience, reducing training time and boosting productivity. 
The chatbot's data accessibility and ease of use have been key 
factors in its success, promoting rapid adoption and efficient 
utilization. 
In terms of limitations, our study was based on a limited 
number of small shops and operational scenarios. While the 
results were promising, the diversity of the shops evaluated 
does not fully represent all possible variations in the industry. 
Additionally, the application evaluation period was short, 
which may not have captured all the seasonal and operational 
variations a small shop may experience over time. 
For future implications, incorporating IoT devices could 
improve product tracking and process automation in small 
shops, revolutionizing inventory management and logistics.

Abstract—Small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) often
operate on limited profit margins. They may lack the financial
resources to implement expensive Enterprise Resource Planning
(ERP) systems or advanced artificial intelligence (AI) tools.
However, the advent of generative AI technologies, such as
GPT-4.5, Grok 3, Gemini 2.0, and DeepSeek R-1, presents an
opportunity for these businesses to leverage AI-driven insights at
a more affordable cost. This paper investigates the effectiveness
of these AI models in addressing key supply chain management
challenges, specifically focusing on demand planning and logistics.
The results provide valuable insights into the most suitable AI
tools for SMBs seeking to optimize their supply chain operations
with minimal investment. This study offers practical guidance
for SMBs to improve operational efficiency and enhance their
competitive edge in the marketplace by conducting a comparative
analysis of these tools.

I. INTRODUCTION
Small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) across the
globe often operate on tight profit margins, with limited
financial resources to invest in expensive Enterprise Resource
Planning (ERP) systems such as SAP or Oracle. Similarly,
sophisticated artificial intelligence (AI) tools like Palantir
Foundry and DataRobot, commonly used by large enterprises,
are often financially inaccessible to many SMBs. However, the
rapid advancement of generative AI technologies, including
GPT-4.5, Grok 3, Gemini 2.0, and DeepSeek R-1, offers
SMBs an opportunity to leverage AI-driven insights at a
reduced cost. Integrating such AI tools into their operations
allows SMBs to make more informed decisions, ultimately
improving revenue and reducing operational costs.
A critical area where AI can assist SMBs is in supply
chain management. Traditionally, supply chain optimization
has relied on complex and costly software solutions, limiting
smaller businesses’ ability to capitalize fully on data-driven
decision-making. However, with the rise of AI, SMBs can
now access advanced analytics and automation capabilities
without significant financial investments. AI applications
in supply chain management encompass various domains,
such as demand planning and logistics. By improving these
functions, businesses can increase efficiency, reduce waste,
optimize inventory levels, and streamline the movement of
goods, thereby strengthening overall competitiveness.
This paper aims to evaluate the effectiveness of several
AI models—GPT-4.5, Grok 3, Gemini 2.0, and DeepSeek R-
1—in addressing key supply chain challenges. Specifically, the
study will assess these AI tools by presenting one question
from each critical domain of supply chain management: de-
mand planning and logistics. The responses generated by these
models will be analyzed to determine which AI tool provides
the most accurate and actionable insights. The findings will
help identify the most suitable AI algorithms for SMBs seek-
ing to optimize their supply chain operations. This comparative
analysis aims to bridge the gap between AI technology and
practical business applications, offering valuable guidance for
SMBs looking for cost-effective solutions to improve supply
chain efficiency while looking at the current capability of these
AI tools.

pressure them to remain competitive. To stay viable, these

advent of generative AI offers SMBs a valuable opportunity

SMBs can enhance decision-making, improve operational

Generative AI models—GPT-4.5, Grok 3, Gemini 2.0, and

in predicting demand. The models’ accuracy is assessed
using the Mean Absolute Percentage Error for the test
dataset (MAPE). Additionally, the recommended machine
learning(ML) models for demand forecasting are analyzed

B. Logistics
None of the artificial intelligence (AI) models evaluated
in this study successfully solved the vehicle routing problem
(VRP), primarily due to the inherent computational complexity
associated with this problem. The VRP involves finding the
most optimal routes for vehicles to deliver goods to various
locations while minimizing costs, a well-known logistics and
supply chain management challenge. Despite the advanced
capabilities of modern AI tools, the computational demands
required to solve VRP instances at scale remain a significant
barrier. This highlights the need for continued advancements
in AI-powered logistics solutions, especially in the context of
small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs), which may face
additional resource constraints.
V. CONCLUSION AND DISCUSSION
The inability of current AI models to effectively address
the VRP points to the need for further advancements in
AI-powered logistics solutions. Future research should focus
on developing more scalable and efficient algorithms to
tackle the VRP and other logistics challenges. Hybrid AI
approaches, which combine multiple AI models or integrate
AI with traditional optimization methods, could be an
effective solution to improve the scalability and efficiency of
logistics operations. Furthermore, AI’s ability to solve VRP
in real-time, under dynamic and changing conditions, remains
a significant area for improvement. Additionally, further
studies should explore larger datasets for demand planning
and implement more examples using k-fold cross-validation
to develop better solutions.
In conclusion, while DeepSeek R-1 demonstrated consid-
erable promise in demand planning, providing SMBs with
a tool to enhance forecasting accuracy and optimize supply
chain operations, the challenge of solving complex logistics
problems, such as the Vehicle Routing Problem, remains
unsolved by current AI models. This study suggests that
SMBs should consider DeepSeek R-1 for demand planning
and inventory management while keeping a close eye on
future advancements in AI for logistics. As AI technology
evolves, these tools have significant potential to support SMBs
in tackling increasingly complex supply chain challenges.
Thus, continued investment in AI research and development
is essential to unlocking its full potential for SMBs across
various supply chain domains.

Abstract— Effective and location-intelligent sales forecasting is 
a strategic requirement within the emerging context of smart 
retail. The approach proposed in this study is a hybrid forecasting 
framework based on Facebook Prophet to achieve a robust time-
series pattern decomposition with XGBoost to capture nonlinear 
effects of sales drivers on the residual. This study uses the 
Rossmann drugstore chain dataset in Germany to predict state-by-
day sales with internal factors (promotions, assortments mix, store 
format) as well as external ones (public holidays, proximity of 
competitors). Strong statistical and machine-learning baselines, 
such as naive, seasonal naive, Holt, Winters and SARIMA, and 
stand-alone Prophet and XGBoost, are benchmarked against the 
hybrid. Results indicate that the proposed algorithm can deliver 
consistent improvements across the 16 German states, cutting 
median state-wise MAPE by 12 - 18% compared to the best non-
hybrid baseline. The framework produces explainable and 
accurate forecasts because it leverages the XGBoost complex 
nonlinearities with the interpretability of Prophet. In addition to 
predictive 
performance, 
the 
model 
has 
region-specific 
explanations: promotional effect, holiday effect, and seasonal 
variation transpose differently across states, which can be used as 
evidenced-based directions when setting inventory, promotional 
schedules, and area network intensification. The results constitute 
a scalable statistically-oriented predictive framework in the 
context of a competitive retailing scenario, and some of its aspects 
are especially new, such as regarding the use of Prophet-XGBoosts 
hybrid in geo-disaggregated pharmaceutical pharmaceutical retail 
sales.

I. 
INTRODUCTION 
 The retail market has changed drastically over the past years 
following the emergence of e-commerce, technological 
advancement, and globalization. Such radical changes have 
rendered retail operations to be very complicated and they need 
precise and swift decision frameworks. Of these, accurate sales 
forecasting has come to play a strategic role in achieving market 
decisions related to marketing, finance, inventory and supply 
chain logistics. Precise and accurate forecasting is associated 
with the opportunity of overstocking or stock-out; both of 
which directly impact profitability and customer satisfaction. 
Retail forecasting process is, however, a non-trivial process due 
to the ever-responsive influences of the external factors which 
include government policies, technological changes, trends in 
consumer preferences and competitive pressure. Forecasting 
models have no assurance that they will come up with reliable 
predictions unless the models can adjust to such conditions. 
Well-established statistical predictive models including Auto-
Regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model, 
exponential smoothing and the Holt-Winters methodology have 
heretofore offered the bedrock within the predictive modeling 
of time-series [1]-[3]. Simultaneously, by using machine 
learning, predictive models, including regression analysis and 
decision trees have been implemented to extract the past sales 
pattern to extrapolate future demand [4], [5]. More 
sophisticated methods such as clustering-based methods and 
artificial neural networks (ANMs) have also enhances the 
accuracy of forecasting [6]-[8]. The work on retail forecasting 
over the last ten years has also illustrated how forecasts are 
commonly generated at the business-wide and product level, 
information which can be used in making business-level 
strategic and operations decisions about product placements, 
pricing, purchases and inventories [9]-[11]. Regardless of these 
methodological advances, the aspect of retail, although 
dynamic, has made the forecast hard because retail is defined 
by government regulation and innovation and consumer 
preferences and the competition. Consequently, retail 
forecasting has become a very important research topic in order 
to empower companies to successfully predict demand and 
align their strategies to meet it.

V. 
DISCUSSION AND RECOMMENDATION 
These findings indicate that the hybrid Prophet and XGBoost 
model outperforms both the classical statistics and the stand-
alone machine learning baselines, with median state-level 
MAPE decreased by 12 to i 8, and estimates both accurate and 
interpretable. The feature importance analysis reveals that 
promotions, assortment type and store format represent the key 
drivers of sales with promotions increasing their weekly sales 
by up to 8 percent in North Rhinewestphalia and only 3 percent 
in Saarland and Extended or Extra assortments consistently 
increasing their sales over Basic assortments by 5-7 percent. 
Regional variation also occurs in store formats, with type B 
stores able to achieve higher sales in the NW and BE and type 
D stores able to achieve higher sales in the TH and HH, and this 
can facilitate the location-specific expansion choices. The 
effects of holidays were modest but significant in the case of 
several states, including BY and SN, and the proper 
consideration of the number of closed days decreased the 
forecasting error by 1520 percent and verified the significance 
of the calendar-conscious planning. According to these 
findings, managers must focus promotions early in the week 
and custom-control intensity by state, expand Extended and 
Extra offerings in high demand states, prioritize the 
introduction of store formats by region, and optimize inventory 
placement to local promotional sensitivity to reduce stock-outs.  
VI. 
CONCLUSION 
Making accurate and efficient sales forecasts is important in the 
retail industry, as a lot of decisions are made based on them. 
Following this forecasting strategy, the company won’t have to 
pay high costs for storing unsold goods and can earn more 
money. This research examined the performance of various 
machine learning algorithms after considering various aspects 
that affect the process. The use of a recent time series technique 
i.e., Facebook Prophet for forecasting sales is investigated. It 
became clear that XGBoost did better in predicting outcomes 
compared to the other models. In the same way, Facebook 
Prophet provided good results. It is necessary to note that this 
technique solely looks at the sales increase connected to the 
regressor. The results from this project could apply to other 
industries where researchers would try out Facebook Prophet.

Abstract—Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) play a 
vital role in supporting Indonesia’s economic growth. However, 
their adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) remains limited 
despite its potential to enhance efficiency, innovation, and 
competitiveness. This study extends the Technology Acceptance 
Model (TAM) to explore how perceived ease of use, perceived 
usefulness, and perceived security influence SMEs’ intention to 
adopt AI technologies. A quantitative approach was employed 
using survey data collected from 131 Indonesian SME owners 
and managers. The data were analyzed using Partial Least 
Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The 
findings reveal that perceived ease of use significantly shapes 
both the perceived usefulness of AI and the intention to adopt it, 
consistent with TAM's theoretical propositions. Interestingly, 
perceived usefulness does not affect substantially adoption 
intention, suggesting that functional benefits alone are 
insufficient to drive adoption in this context. Instead, perceived 
security emerges as a critical determinant, indicating that SMEs 
place strong emphasis on data protection, privacy, and system 
reliability when considering AI implementation. This study 
contributes to refining the TAM framework by highlighting the 
central role of security as a determinant of adoption behavior 
and demonstrating the limited influence of perceived usefulness 
in high-risk technological settings. The results underscore the 
need for policymakers and technology providers to prioritize 
secure and accessible AI solutions to foster inclusive and 
sustainable digital transformation among Indonesian SMEs.

I. INTRODUCTION  
Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) are essential to 
Indonesia's economic growth, as they employ the bulk of the 
country's workforce and account for more than 60% of its 
GDP [1]. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a key 
technology that may improve competitiveness, efficiency, and 
decision-making in the age of rapid digital transformation. 
Adopting AI is now essential for Indonesian SMEs to prosper 
in increasingly globalized and dynamic marketplaces, not just 
a luxury [2]. 
However, Indonesian SMEs continue to deploy AI 
technologies unevenly, with several obstacles. Technology 
acceptability, which includes managers' and entrepreneurs' 
readiness to incorporate AI technologies into their business 
operations, is one of the most critical elements affecting 
adoption [3]. Perceptions of usability, compatibility with 
current systems, and ease of use influence this adoption. 
Security is also critical because worries about data privacy, 
cyber risks, and regulatory compliance greatly impact trust 
and the desire to use AI breakthroughs [4]. 
An unusual setting for studying these processes is 
Indonesia. Government programs like Making Indonesia 4.0 
and the acceleration of the development of the digital 
economy are driving the nation's rapid increases in internet 
adoption and digital literacy [5]. SMEs' limitations may 
hamper the implementation of AI in infrastructure, 
knowledge, and resources. Therefore, creating strategies that 
help SMEs leverage AI for sustained growth requires an 
understanding of how security perceptions and technology 
acceptability influence AI adoption behavior. 
Recent scholarship on AI and technology adoption in 
SMEs has identified multiple factors shaping successful 
implementation. Within the Technology–Organization–
Environment (TOE) framework [6], drivers such as relative 
advantage, compatibility, human capital, market demand, and 
government support emerge as critical, with evidence 
suggesting that medium-sized firms benefit more strongly 
from relative advantage than smaller firms [7]. Similarly, 
research using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of 
Technology (UTAUT) model shows that effort expectancy 
and social influence significantly affect behavioral intention 
to adopt generative AI, with age and work experience 
moderating these effects [8]. Leadership has also been shown 
to influence AI adoption through fostering data-driven 
cultures and enhancing employee competencies, which in turn 
strengthen supply chain resilience [9]. Yet, in many 
developing country contexts, SMEs continue to rely primarily 
on basic information systems rather than advanced 
technologies such as AI, underscoring the importance of 
sociocultural and contextualized adoption models [10]. 
Building upon the preceding discussion, this study offers 
a novel contribution by examining technology acceptance and 
security perceptions concurrently as determinants of AI 
adoption intention among Indonesian SMEs, a sector 
experiencing rapid digital transformation yet marked by 
uneven technological uptake. The Technology Acceptance 
Model (TAM) serves as the central theoretical framework for 
elucidating user behavior toward emerging technologies,

II. LITERATURE REVIEW 
Grounded in the constructs of perceived usefulness and 
perceived ease of use, the Technology Acceptance Model 
(TAM) provides a structured framework for understanding 
how individuals and organizations form intentions to engage 
with emerging technologies. When integrated with the Theory 
of Planned Behavior, TAM has demonstrated strong 
explanatory power, accounting for approximately 59% of the 
variance in AI acceptance across various contexts [11]. Its 
adaptability has been evident in multiple domains. For 
instance, in the hospitality and tourism industry, the 
development of an interactive TAM (iTAM) highlights the 
critical role of perceived interactivity in shaping user attitudes 
toward AI-enabled service robots [12]. Similarly, studies 
combining TAM with status quo bias theory in the context of 
AI voice assistants show that perceived ease of use and 
perceived value positively influence user attitudes, whereas 
switching costs and perceived risks act as barriers to adoption 
[13]. In the education sector, TAM has been employed to 
examine teachers’ intentions to utilize AI-based e-learning 
platforms, revealing that perceptions of usefulness and 
emotional 
engagement 
significantly 
impact 
adoption 
decisions [14]. Collectively, these findings underscore TAM’s 
relevance as a theoretical lens for exploring how perceptions 
of utility, usability, and security interact to shape AI adoption 
behaviors—particularly in dynamic, resource-constrained 
environments such as SMEs. 
Studies investigating the impact of Perceived Ease of Use 
(PEU) on AI adoption intentions (IAI) demonstrate 
consistently favorable correlations across several areas. In 
accounting education, PEU serves as a mediator between 
technological preparedness and aspirations to use AI, in 
conjunction with perceived utility [15]. Likewise, PEU has 
substantial positive effects on both the desire to use and the 
actual adoption of digital technologies, such as e-wallets [16]. 
In the realm of AI-enabled smart speakers, PEU is a pivotal 
aspect impacting attitudes and intentions for continued usage, 
whereas social elements such as media richness and parasocial 
interactions shape perceptions of PEU [17]. These results 
repeatedly validate PEU as an essential determinant in AI 
adoption across different contexts and user demographics. 
[18] discovered that in small and medium firms in Taiwan, 
only perceived ease of use (PEU) had a direct impact on 
perceived usefulness (PU), and PU was the only direct 
predictor of system utilization. This is different from the 
original TAM research by [19], which revealed that PU had a 
significant effect on user intentions, whereas PEU had a 
weaker but still significant effect that weakened over time. 
The positive correlation between PEU and PU has been 
consistently validated across several areas. [20] validated that 
PEU substantially influences PU in the context of e-book 
uptake among university students. [15] also discovered that 
both PEU and PU act as intermediaries in the interaction 
between technological readiness and the adoption of artificial 
intelligence in accounting contexts, demonstrating their 
ongoing significance in contemporary technology acceptance 
frameworks. 
PU acts as a bridge between students' readiness to use 
technology and their plans to use AI [15]. In the same way, 
studies of employees demonstrate that PU completely 
mediates the negative link between job instability and plans to 
use AI, and somewhat mediates the positive link between 
habit and plans to utilize AI at work [21]. PU affects more than 
only AI-specific applications. For example, research on the 
adoption of e-wallets demonstrates that PU has a significant 
beneficial impact on both usage intentions and actual adoption 
behaviors [16]. In AI assistant-enabled smart speakers, 
perceived usefulness (PU) is a significant factor that affects 
how users feel about the technology and whether they plan to 
keep using it. It works with the perceived simplicity of use to 
encourage people to adopt the technology [22]. These results 
consistently affirm PU as a critical factor in technology 
adoption decisions. 
In the realm of financial services, technical optimism 
enhances the intention to utilize AI-driven robo-advisors, but 
insecurity diminishes adoption intentions; conversely, 
technological discomfort unexpectedly had good outcomes 
[23]. In terms of security issues, insecurity makes people think 
that AI systems are not very beneficial, especially in retail 
settings, where being inventive and optimistic makes both 
PEOU and PU go up [24]. These findings indicate that security 
concerns and feelings of unease consistently act as obstacles 
to AI adoption across diverse fields.

Abstract— Food consumption is increasing significantly on global 
stage due to social and economic growth, leading to higher food 
production and development in food supply chain (FSC). Many 
firms have been adopting artificial intelligence (AI) in FSC to deal 
with problems. This research aims to investigate the influence of 
AI technology adoption of micro, small, and medium enterprise 
(MSME) FSC in aspect of traceability and transparency in 
Thailand. As various statistical research discussed in the 
introduction section points out that nowadays FSC still lack of 
traceability and transparency, which affects to product 
consumption of customers. A quantitative approach through an 
online questionnaire is utilized to gather statistical data, along 
with conducting the literature review from existing literatures. 92 
of MSMEs in Thailand are used as a sample for this research then 
linear regression is applied for data analysis. The result of the 
study indicates that AI significantly influences firm’s performance 
in term of traceability and transparency. AI facilitates in sourcing, 
production, scheduling, and transportation. It provides a better 
decision making and ensures that all processes in FSC reach 
standards. However, there are some limitations in technology 
adoption for MSMEs specifically in micro businesses as they still 
lack know-how and budget for technological investment. 
Index Terms—Food supply chain, artificial intelligence, 
traceability, transparency, MSME 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Over 8.1 billion people at present globally, food production 
and consumption have become way more significant issue 
comparing to the past. The main goal of the food industry is to 
provide good foods and other necessities that is suitable for the 
diversity of human’s activities and lifestyle. In order to serve 
the expanding population, the method of interconnected 
activities that operate in the food supply chain (FSC) must be 
transformed significantly [1]. FSC refers to all complex 
networks between farm and processing activities, distributors, 
and retailers that operate the concept of ‘farm to fork’ [2]. The 
process begins by the raw material until final products are 
delivered to customers. [2] employed a systematic review on 
challenges in FSC. The result indicates the three most common 
issues in FSC, including sustainability, food safety and quality, 
traceability, and transparency. Among three issues, traceability 
and transparency gains the lowest percentage of distribution in 
term of being mentioned by articles [2], implying that 
traceability and transparency still do not gain much attention in 
majority comparing to other two issues, although it is an 
important topic. FSC with a lack of traceability and 
transparency will adversely impact the efficiency on FSC [3]. 
Nowadays food trade becomes globalized, food chain integrity 
is not concerning only about food safety but also with its origin 
[4]. In most region, most academic research in firm’s 
performance highlighted more on large firms rather than a small 
and medium firm [5]. Although MSMEs are a core economic 
driver in many countries, but still become neglected compared 
to large firm. Particularly in Thailand, MSMEs play a vital role 
in the Thai economy contributing to 35.2% of the total gross 
domestic product (GDP). MSMEs generated GDP value as 
amounting to 1,784,473 million baht, representing 39.97% of 
the GDP in manufacturing sector as a whole [6]. These 
statistical data implies that Thai MSMEs is an important part in 
Thai economy and should be gained more attention from many 
departments. 
      Nowadays traceability and transparency issue, tracking and 
tracing technology is still not widely standardized. Outdated 
technologies and traditional manual methods can cause a lack of 
traceability. [7] had addressed some barriers to AI adoption in 
FSC. The challenge for AI adoption is due to lacking an 
appropriate testing system or trial facilities of AI technology, 
especially in the scope of our study, MSMEs. Local MSMEs still 
do not have the readiness to become fully invested in 
technology. Therefore, this research aims to examine the 
influence of AI technology adoption in FSC on MSMEs’ 
business performance in aspect of traceability and transparency, 
along with studying the gap that may occur for the adoption. 
II. LITERATURE REVIEW 
A. Food Supply Chain 
FSC is the network of several members who participate in 
the transformation of raw materials and semi-finished products 
to final foods delivered to consumers [8]. FSC involves in 
combination of processes and operations which aim to 
transform raw products from their original source to final food 
products consumed by customers [9]. The process of FSC

B. Food Traceability and Transparency 
[12] defined food traceability as part of logistic 
management which captures, stores, and transfers information 
about food in the entire stages of FSC so that products can be 
verified to control quality and safety, tracked forwardly, and 
traced backwardly at any time required. Three main processes 
are required for a tracking system in FSC, including the 
transformation of analog data to digital data, transmission of 
digital data from a local source to the database, lastly the user 
assess and collaboration [13]. Transparency refers to the 
disclosure of a product’s information, such as production 
process, ingredients, environmental and social impacts, 
certification, label that indicates the product’s quality and so on 
[14]. [13] mentioned that the major cause of food 
contamination is from lack of traceability and transparency. As 
food takes a long path from producer to customer, food 
contamination can occur easily at any stage of FSC leading to a 
negative domino effect. Once it happens, it takes a long time to 
point out the exact source and reason of contamination and 
specifically identify the contaminated products. This issue can 
become a crucial concern to all members in FSC, especially 
those who are still lacking digital and technology skills [4]. 
C. Artificial Intelligence  
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a sub-field of computer science 
involving with creation of innovative machines and computer 
systems that can perform any task which requires human 
intelligence [15]. These innovations have the potential to 
directly impact both the manufacturing processes and the details 
of several products and services, with important implications for 
productivity, employment, and competition [16].  [17] employed 
a systematic review of AI applications in supply chain and 
classified AI according to their techniques into four sub-fields. 
First sub-field includes Artificial neural network and Rough set 
theory. The second sub-field includes Machine learning, Expert 
systems and Genetic algorithms. The third sub-field includes 
Fuzzy logic. Lastly, forth sub-field includes Agent-based 
systems. This study is going to highlight on the outstanding AI 
techniques based on the result of application in the supply chain 
and adapting to FSC for this study. According to the result from 
[17], machine learning is the most dominant type of AI that has 
been used throughout all processes in supply chain. Genetic 
algorithm is the second most used type of AI which is used in 
five out of six processes in supply chain. Artificial neural 
network, Expert system, Fuzzy logic, and Agent-based system 
are applied in three processes. However, only ANN is engaged 
in purchasing and procurement, production, and inventory 
management which are core processes that directly affect the 
product’s quality and major management in all supply chain. 
Therefore, this study will highlight three potential AI sub-fields, 
including machine learning, genetic algorithm, and artificial 
neural network 
a) Machine Learning: Machine learning (ML) is a subset 
of AI that facilitates the system to be capable of identifying 
patterns and making decision by learning and improving from 
experience and previous data set without being programmed 
[18]. Algorithms are trained using a large collection of two data 
groups, the training set and the testing set. The algorithm will 
receive a set of inputs with correct outputs, known as pre-
labeled information, to compare its actual output with correct 
outputs and spot errors [19]. Regression is an example of 
machine learning that will be applied to this research. 
Regression is used to determine a relationship between the 
independent variable and the dependent variable. It instructs a 
model using a dataset of X and Y and uses the trained model to 
predict the output of new input data [26].  
b) Genetic Algorithm: Genetic algorithm (GA) refers to 
the principle of natural selection and agorithms inspired by the 
biological evolution of living beings [20]. The fittest 
chromosome will survive to generate new offspring, and this 
process is replicated for multiple generations [21]. The weaker 
chromosome will be eliminated. This technique is used for 
optimization problems by finding the maximum or minimum 
value. [22]. There are five components in GA, which are 
chromosome representation, selection, crossover, mutation, and 
fitness function computation [23]. Selection, crossover, and 
mutation are considered as three core operations in GA. 
Selection is where a chromosome in the population will be in a 
structure that hold information related to a potential solution 
with a combination of weights [24]. Crossover is to combine 
chromosomes of two parent to produce new offspring that is 
phenotypically like the parents [25]. Mutation is proformed 
intentionally to stop falling of all solution in the population to 
an optimal level of the solved problem [21].
